records.quote: Proposition 2.I: Let F1 (x; α, β, θ) and G1 (x; α, β, θ) be the cdfs of the EPAD and EWD, each with parameters ∝, β and θ. Then F1 (x; α, β, θ) ≤ G1 (x; α, β, θ). That is the EPAD (α, β, θ) exhibits first-order stochastic dominance over the EWD (α, β, θ).
records.family: Exponentiated Power Affine... EPAD(α, β, θ) vs exponentiated Weibull EWD(α, β, θ), common parameters
records.compared: EPAD vs EWD at identical parameter values

hypotheses.text: F1 and G1 each with parameters α, β, θ
hypotheses.formal: common parameter values across the two cdfs

conclusion.direction: EPAD >=st EWD (F1(x) <= G1(x) for all x; EWD side smaller)

records.quantifiers: all x (trivially for x < 0; proof uses 1 + θx^β >= 0 for x >= 0)
records.ambiguity: Printed as 'Proposition 2.I'; proof shows F1 = [1−(1+θx^β)e^{−θx^β}]^α <= [1−e^{−θx^β}]^α = G1.

note: Paper prints F1 <= G1 pointwise with EPAD first-order stochastically dominating EWD — Y/EWD side smaller; A's 'A_smaller' flag misread the CDF inequality.
